title: Usage & Billing Forensics + QBR Action Plan
content:
Purpose: Compact worksheet for conducting a rapid forensic-style review of token spend, rate-limit incidents, and budget alerts ahead of a Quarterly Business Review (QBR). Use this during the 30–45 minute pre-QBR run-through to surface anomalies, mitigation history, and concrete renewal-facing recommendations.

How to use:
- Step 1: Populate the Metrics Snapshot table with the last 90 days (or since last QBR).
- Step 2: Walk anomalies and incidents chronologically; add root-cause hypotheses and evidence links.
- Step 3: Confirm current alert thresholds and escalation contacts.
- Step 4: Decide 2–3 action items to discuss during the QBR (owner + target date).

Section A — QBR Snapshot
- Customer: Acme Retail (example row)
- QBR period: 2025-11-01 to 2026-01-31
- Account owner (CS): Jordan Patel
- Renewal window: 2026-04-15 to 2026-05-15
- Contract: Dedicated reserved (monthly commit)
- Impact band: mid-enterprise (projected annual spend $120k)

Section B — Metrics Snapshot (last 90 days)
- Total tokens consumed (all models): 48,320,451 tokens
- Avg tokens / request: 1,142 tokens
- Peak tokens / minute: 1,120,000 tokens (2026-01-09 14:22 UTC)
- Avg latency p50/p95: 32ms / 210ms
- # of rate-limit events: 5 (see incident timeline)
- # of budget-alert triggers: 3 (thresholds crossed on dates below)
- Top 3 endpoints by volume: /chat.generate (64%), /embed.create (22%), /completion (14%)

Section C — Anomaly & Incident Timeline (chronological)
1) 2025-11-18 09:12 UTC — sudden token spike +120% vs baseline
   - Magnitude: +1.8M tokens in 30m window
   - Immediate effect: transient 429s for some requests, auto-retry increased overall spend
   - Evidence: request_id trace CON-2589, logs in S3://acme-logs/2025-11-18/*
   - Hypothesis: background batch job re-run after deploy; missing idempotency key
   - Actions taken: temporary rate cap applied (CS + infra), developer notified, batch fix deployed 2025-11-19
   - Notes for QBR: demonstrate improved safeguards (idempotency + blocking rule) and ask about scheduled jobs visibility

2) 2025-12-23 03:30 UTC — repeated budget alerts during holiday test
   - Magnitude: three alerts in 24 hours at 80% budget threshold
   - Root cause: internal QA load and external test harness left running by partner team
   - Mitigation: CS helped pause keys, implemented a partner-specific quota, scheduled follow-up meeting with partner ops

3) 2026-01-09 14:22 UTC — peak throughput incident
   - Symptoms: high p95 latency and short 503 bursts (approx 2 minutes)
   - Evidence: serving-runtime trace ID SR-7331, autoscale metric shows pod spin-up lag
   - Hypothesis: burst exceeded pre-warmed pool size; autoscale policy conservatively configured for cost
   - Short-term fix: temporarily bumped burst pool for business-hours window; long-term: recommend modified autoscale rule + burst buffer in Dedicated contract

Section D — Rate Limit & Alert Configuration (current)
- Account-level rate cap: 60 requests / sec sustained; burst allowance 120 r/s for 30s
- Budget alert thresholds: 50% (info), 80% (action), 95% (escalate) -> current escalation: email -> slack -> pager (on-call)
- Notification owners: billing@acme.com, platform-leads@acme.com, cs-jordan@redwood.ai

Section E — Recommended Adjustments (engineer + commercial trade-offs)
- Short-term (recommended before QBR)
  - Lower developer integration keys to 10 r/s by default; create partner-specific quota at 5k r/s for production workloads (impact: may require partner coordination)
  - Adjust budget alert to add a daily digest at 40% and link to self-serve runway calculator (low friction)
- Medium-term (1–2 quarters)
  - Add prefix caching for the top 5 heavy endpoints (expected savings ~18% tokens)
  - Change autoscale policy to pre-warm 2 extra pods for known peak windows (reduces 503s, adds ~3–5% infra cost)
- Commercial conversation suggestions for renewal
  - Offer a burst-protection add-on (monthly fee) to secure predictable latency for seasonal peaks
  - Propose a 10% commit increase in exchange for a 7% discount and 45-day runbook review (tie to joint SLAs)

Section F — QBR Talking Points (for CS lead)
- Quick success: reduced post-spike spend after idempotency fix; show before/after token curve
- Current risk: partner test harness and no separate partner quota -> propose partner quota step
- Ask for decision: approve burst-protection pilot or accept small commit increase
- Operational ask: name 1 defender (platform contact) to be included in weekly incident digests

Section G — Action Item Tracker (pick 2–3 for QBR commitment)
- AI-1: Create partner quota and set dev/test keys to restricted mode — Owner: Priya Sharma — Due: 2026-02-28 — Status: in progress
- AI-2: Implement daily budget digest + runway calculator link — Owner: Ethan Rivera — Due: 2026-03-05 — Status: todo
- AI-3: Propose burst-protection pilot pricing sheet for renewal pack — Owner: Jordan Patel — Due: 2026-03-01 — Status: draft

Appendix A — Quick checklist before presenting
- Attach token consumption graph (90-day) + incident markers (image or link)
- Confirm alert contact list is up to date in billing console
- Prepare one slide showing cost savings from caching suggestion (approx math included)

Appendix B — Example quick math (savings estimate)
- If prefix caching reduces token count by 18%, expected tokens = 48,320,451 * 0.82 = ~39.6M tokens -> approx $Xk saved / quarter (insert price-per-token here)

Notes / loose thoughts (scratchpad):
- Could we offer a low-friction toggle in Console to ‘lock dev keys’ for accounts nearing renewal?
- Consider a small automated runbook that downgrades partner keys when budget alert hits 95% and notifies both teams

Evidence links / artifacts to attach in final QBR:
- S3 logs (link), Confluence incident write-ups (CONFLUENCE-CC/usage-templates), JIRA CS-4521 (partner quota task), internal playbook PR #298
